case.believed: page.$$eval passes one matching element like page.$eval, missing selectors fail the same way in both APIs, DOM nodes returned from page.evaluate serialize as ordinary objects, and a synchronous function exposed from Node remains synchronous in the page.
contract: page.$$eval passes an array of matching elements to its callback; treating the first argument as one element reads undefined, while mapping the array returns every text value.
page.$eval rejects when no element matches, whereas page.$$eval calls its callback with an empty array and returns normally.
Returning document.body directly from page.evaluate crosses the protocol as an empty plain object rather than a serialized DOM node.
A synchronous Node function installed with page.exposeFunction returns a Promise in the browser context and yields its value only when awaited.
The complete contract runs in the pinned Chrome 134 browser with the container network disabled.
case.goal: Verify Puppeteer 24.4.0 page.$eval, page.$$eval, page.evaluate, and page.exposeFunction callback and serialization boundaries in a real offline Chrome 134 context.
